https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Labor member for Chifley, Ed Husic, was taken to hospital with significant injuries after his car was hit by a truck on a Sydney motorway View image in fullscreen Labor member for Chifley, Ed Husic, was taken to hospital with significant injuries after his car was hit by a truck on a Sydney motorway Labor party Labor MP Ed Husic taken to hospital with fractures and concussion after car crash Husic to take ‘short’ period of leave after collision on Sydney motorway on Tuesday Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Tom McIlroy Political editor Wed 5 Aug 2026 18.52 EDT Last modified on Wed 5 Aug 2026 19.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Labor MP Ed Husic was hospitalised this week after his car was involved in an accident with a truck travelling on Sydney’s M7 motorway. The incident happened when the Chifley MP was travelling home from his electorate office, around 6.20pm on Tuesday, according to a spokesperson. Husic was treated by paramedics at the scene and taken to hospital for assessment and treatment. He was discharged on Wednesday with minor abrasions, fractures and a concussion. A spokesperson for the MP said he was providing a statement to police about the incident. “On medical advice, Mr Husic will take a short period of leave from parliamentary duties while he recovers. “Mr Husic thanked the doctors, nurses and paramedics at Westmead Hospital for providing him with outstanding care and thanked his friends and family for their support, especially during his hospital stay.” Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Photos of the car show serious damage to the back driver’s side, with windows and windscreens smashed and airbags deployed. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks Preview latest after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen The car Labor MP Ed Husic was driving in during Tuesday’s accident in Sydney Husic, the former industry minister, is expected to return to parliamentary duties soon. Parliament resumes in Canberra on Tuesday after the July winter break. “Mr Husic was extremely grateful to walk away from the accident without more serious injury,” the spokesperson said. NSW police have been contacted about the incident. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: A fur seal, similar to this one seen sleeping in New Zealand, is the first confirmed mammal death from the deadly H5 bird flu strain on the Australian mainland. Photograph: David C Tomlinson/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A fur seal, similar to this one seen sleeping in New Zealand, is the first confirmed mammal death from the deadly H5 bird flu strain on the Australian mainland. Photograph: David C Tomlinson/Getty Images Bird flu Fur seal‘s death marks first Australian mainland mammal fatality from spreading H5 bird flu strain Seal found dead at Beachport in South Australia on Wednesday follows three mass mortality events in terns Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Lisa Cox Sat 22 Aug 2026 20.42 EDT Last modified on Sat 22 Aug 2026 20.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A long-nosed fur seal has died from H5 bird flu in South Australia, marking the first confirmed case in a mammal on the Australian mainland. The seal was found dead at Beachport on Wednesday on the state’s Limestone Coast. It marks a fresh escalation in the spread of the virus days after the South Australian premier, Peter Malinauskas, announced three mass mortality events on offshore islands involving more than 1,000 greater crested terns. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email The highly pathogenic strain of bird flu has killed millions of birds globally and crossed over into mammal species, including elephant seals . Long-nosed fur seals and the endangered Australian sea lion are among the mammal species the federal government has assessed as facing very high risk from the virus. The SA government has also confirmed a little penguin found at Kangaroo Island this week also tested positive for H5 bird flu. More to come. https://www.politico.eu/article/ursula-v.text: Greenland is making a “clear choice” to strengthen ties with the EU, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Monday, as Brussels unveiled a €200 million investment package and moved to deepen its political, economic and security footprint in the Arctic. Speaking in Nuuk alongside Greenlandic Premier Jens-Frederik Nielsen and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, von der Leyen cast the relationship as a two-way partnership. The renewed EU-Greenland declaration, she said, “reflects a clear choice expressed by Greenland to strengthen ties with the European Union,” while also demonstrating Europe’s own decision “to be more present” and more engaged in Greenland and across the Arctic. Advertisement Advertisement U.S. President Donald Trump has made repeated threats to take over Greenland. In July, he said that “Greenland … should be controlled by the United States, not by Denmark” at the outset of a NATO summit in Turkey. The Arctic has rapidly climbed up Brussels’ geopolitical agenda. Von der Leyen said the region had become a place “where the tectonic plates of geopolitics collide,” adding that the EU has a direct stake in developments there and is preparing a new Arctic strategy for presentation this fall. The Arctic is also expected to feature prominently in von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech next week, as Brussels prepares the revamped strategy. She also reiterated that Greenland’s future is for the people of Greenland and Denmark to decide. The two-day visit, which began Sunday, was aimed at turning the political message into concrete projects. A Commission official said the trip had been months in the making but was postponed at Frederiksen’s request due to Danish elections in March. Von der Leyen signed a renewed joint declaration with Greenland and Denmark and unveiled a €200 million EU partnership package for this year and next. Advertisement Advertisement At Greenlandic telecom operator Tusass, she launched a satellite connectivity project designed to improve internet access in remote communities. Brussels will also support hydropower development and work with Greenland on mining projects intended to more closely link the island’s raw materials to European industry. The broader declaration expands cooperation into education, infrastructure, fisheries, tourism, housing, research, climate action, civil protection, cybersecurity and Arctic resilience. Von der Leyen also pointed to the longer-term relationship, saying the Commission has proposed more than doubling EU funding for Greenland to €530 million through 2034.

https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/se.text: No BS … Better Go Mad in the Wild View image in fullscreen No BS … Better Go Mad in the Wild Movies Review Better Go Mad in the Wild review – boozing, bantering hermits impart their spiritual wisdom Director Miro Remo journeys deep into the Czech countryside to find two brothers living an isolated life filled with quixotic wisdom in this surreal documentary Phil Hoad Tue 8 Sep 2026 02.00 EDT Last modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 02.03 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google N arrated by a slaughtered bull, this extraordinary film takes the less-travelled path in charting the daily life of a pair of Czech twins a long way off conventional routes themselves. František and Ondřej Klišík are slowly going mad – or maybe closing in on enlightenment – in a cabin in the Šumava mountains and, extrapolating a short story about the brothers by Aleš Palán, director Miro Remo succumbs productively to the prevailing cabin fever – not only egging these longbeards on in their squabbling and loopy philosophising, but pitching in with his own fabulism and surrealism. Closing on 60, “Franta” and “Ondra” still farm their smallholding with the help of Nandy, a mutinous bull ill-chosen as a draught animal. In their downtime, they booze, banter and bicker, lament their lack of prospects with the fairer sex, and blow off steam in epic arm-wrestling bouts. Despite an arm lost to a sawmill accident, it’s Franta who’s usually the victor; he is also possessed by a quixotic streak absent in his bluff sibling. Letting loose streams of poetry into the air like bunting, wishing “joy to all conscious beings”, he is also constructing his own Da Vinci-style perpetual flying machine. “Your aversion to my perpetuum is a little annoying,” he informs the exasperated Ondra. The Klišíks are definitely not “boring cunts”, as they dub 99% of humanity (including Vladimir Putin). They were decorated by the Czech state for their anti-Soviet activism, but that engagement seems to have waned, and Remo follows them away from the political deep into the personal and spiritual. In an intense communion with nature, including the animals they kill, they seem to inhabit a strange prelapsarian haven, inside which discord is continually bubbling up. Franta slates Ondra for his alcoholism, into which he is drawn; they differ on which one of them is Cain and which is Abel. In the end, they settle: they’re both Abel. As these spats recur and resolve themselves in kitchen-table laughter, it’s like watching some natural dialectical process in motion; a dishevelled but beautiful ying-yang cohabitation. The twins are ready collaborators in their own mythologisation, participating in Remo’s more leftfield plays, such as sequences where Ondra sledgehammers through the spiral mural on the wall between their rooms, or a dream featuring a levitating Franta. But shortly after the film won the Grand Prix at Karlovy Vary film festival last year, Franta died in a village pond. This took self-mythologisation too far, but his mystical remit still stands though; there is copious wisdom regarding family, nature, interdependency and love in this rowdy, rapturous and brilliant film.
